speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: When Town Councils were formed in 1989, the intent was to give elected Members of Parliament (MPs) the autonomy and latitude to run their own towns.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: MPs were empowered to engage residents directly, understand their concerns and work with them to shape their living environment.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Each town could then develop a distinctive character of its own, under their MP's stewardship.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: In turn, MPs would be directly accountable to their constituents for their performance, through the ballot box.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: To quote then First Deputy Prime Minister Mr Goh Chok Tong at the Parliamentary debate in 1988, I quote, "This Bill will contribute to the attainment of the two philosophical objectives.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: First, it transfers some powers from HDB to the MPs and grassroots leaders.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: It gives them, and the residents, greater power and responsibility to manage their own affairs and to participate in their estate's development.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Second, because MPs will have increased authority and responsibility, voters will be more likely to vote carefully and sincerely and choose honest and effective MPs." Mr Goh Chok Tong added that the formation of Town Councils would provide political parties without any track record with a platform to prove their mettle.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: To quote him, "If a party can manage Town Councils well, it will prove its competence in at least one area − good administration – which is the prerequisite of any government." Mdm Speaker, the raison detre of Town Councils remains relevant today.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Through Town Councils, MPs and Town Councillors have partnered residents to shape their living environment, respond to residents' needs and enhance their sense of belonging to the community.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: However, over the past 28 years, we have learnt useful lessons from the management and operations of Town Councils.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Residents' expectations of their Town Councils have also risen.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: They expect greater accountability and better performance, especially in areas, such as estate cleanliness and maintenance, where the results are visible and immediate.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: But the challenge lies in less tangible areas, like financial management and corporate governance.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: These are just as important, if not more, given the potential downstream impact of financial insolvency and loss of public funds if Town Councils are not managed well.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: But governance lapses and poor management of a Town Council's finances could remain unnoticed until much later, when significant damage or losses have already occurred.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Ultimately, residents are the ones who will be saddled with the consequences.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: So, residents have a right to expect responsible governance from their Town Councils.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: As public institutions entrusted with millions of dollars received from residents and the Government, Town Councils should be held to at least the same standards of governance as charities and public-listed companies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: As the former Minister for National Development Mr Khaw Boon Wan said in Parliament in 2015, MND can no longer take a light-touch approach and assume that the people running Town Councils will all be responsible.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: There is a need to ensure proper systems, accountability and governance to safeguard residents' interests.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: For instance, Town Councils may take the easy way out − make short-term, populist measures, such as lowering service and conservancy charges (S&CC), at the expense of their long-term financial health and the well-being of residents.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We have also seen in recent years serious deficiencies in some Town Councils' governance and financial systems as well as regulatory breaches, but there were few direct levers to put things right.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: While most Town Councils have been cooperative, MND has limited powers under the current Town Councils Act to look into suspected irregularities or enforce the rules set out in the Act if they are not complied with.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Town Councils will continue to manage our Towns autonomously and can decide how best to serve their residents' interests.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: But the Act will establish the required standards of transparency, public accountability and performance for Town Councils and provide for more effective oversight of Town Councils to safeguard the interests of residents.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: As early as 2013, we engaged all the Town Councils on key proposals that would impact their operations, such as financial sustainability and Town Council handover arrangements.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The Lift Replacement Fund in this Bill addresses a shared concern raised at one of these sessions, on the long-term adequacy of Town Councils' Sinking Funds.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Over the last few years, we have heard from Members through debates in this House on Town Council-related issues.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We have also received feedback from members of the public on these matters through letters to MND or HDB or to the media and, more recently, in October last year, MND held a month-long public consultation on the proposed amendments in the Bill.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: All Town Council chairmen were also invited to provide their feedback on the proposed amendments.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The feedback that was received and MND's responses to them were also published online.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We would like to thank Members of this House and the public for all their contributions and feedback.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We have carefully considered all the views and incorporated them, where appropriate, in the process of drafting this amendment Bill.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: First, the Bill clarifies the roles and functions of Town Councils.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Clause 11 reiterates that the Town Councils' core function is to manage the common property of their towns and emphasises that Town Councils are to do so for the benefit of their residents.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: In relation to this, the Bill sets out to clarify some areas that are not explicit in the current Act.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: First and foremost, Town Councils have a duty of care to their residents.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Such activities include setting up subsidiary companies to carry out commercial activities which are not related to their core function to manage common property.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Town Councils are clearly not set up for these purposes and residents should not be made to bear the uncertainties and business risks associated with such commercial ventures.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Some Town Councils have asked if this restriction extends to the fund investments that Town Councils currently carry out to counter inflation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Town Councils can still invest their funds, subject to guidelines under the Town Councils Financial Rules (TCFRs) that limit risk exposure.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Second, Town Councils do not own the common property and neither is their power unfettered.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Under the existing Act, Town Councils may already set and collect charges but only for uses prescribed by MND and are not entitled already to charge HDB for the use of common property.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This will continue to be the case going forward.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Another area that the Bill will clarify is the Town Councils' relationships and interactions with HDB and other statutory authorities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: First, as the owner of common property in HDB estates, HDB has landowner rights, including the use and access to common property.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Clause 29 reaffirms the status of HDB as landowner and emphasises that Town Councils must not perform their functions or exercise their powers in a way that is inconsistent with HDB's title and rights as landowner.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Second, Town Councils are subordinate to public law.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: They cannot hamper statutory authorities carrying out their statutory functions to ensure public health, safety and order, or undertaking works, for instance, Smart Nation initiatives, to improve the quality of life of residents in and around the town.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: If a Town Council unreasonably delays, hampers or obstructs the work of the agency or its officers despite receiving ample notice, the agency may have to, with HDB's consent as landlord, issue a notice to the Town Council, and non-compliance with the notice without reasonable excuse will be made an offence.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Lastly, the Bill will make it clear that Town Councils have a role to play during public emergencies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Where reasonable, MND may provide grants or reimbursements to Town Councils to defray costs incurred.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: I should emphasise that the provisions I just described merely spell out what is already expected of all Town Councils today.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: They do not curtail the broad autonomy and latitude that Town Councils currently enjoy.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The amendments give Town Councils greater clarity on the activities that are part of their core functions and those that are not.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Town Councils should focus on their core function of managing HDB estates and not take on unnecessary commercial and financial risks that detract from their core mission.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: At the same time, there is no reason why Town Councils, HDB and other public agencies should not work collaboratively to further residents' interest, or to safeguard public health, public safety and public order.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Next, let me move on to provisions that improve Town Councils' governance and accountability to residents.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The issue of governance of Town Councils has been a subject of much discussion and cause for concern, as seen from recent events.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This House has spoken unanimously and agreed on the need to strengthen the legislative framework for Town Councils, and the question is how and by how much.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: As a regulator, MND seeks to promote good governance, without unduly hampering the Town Councils' operations and autonomy.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The first suite of enhancements seeks greater transparency and public accountability from Town Councils by raising the standard of disclosure on three fronts: (a) key personnel appointments, (b) financial reporting and (c) Town Councils' compliance with other governance standards.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Town Councils will be required to notify the public and MND of key personnel changes within the Town Council, through amendments to clause 10.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Clause 9 of the Bill clarifies the definition and treatment of conflicts of interest scenarios.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The new section 15A extends conflict disclosure requirements beyond Town Councillors, to committee members, employees of the Town Council or anyone who is delegated with the responsibilities of the Town Council.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This will better manage any risk of conflicts that may arise in Town Councils' management and operations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The Town Council Secretary will be required by law to keep a register of all conflict disclosures.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Town Councils are also required to publish the statements for public access and viewing.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: It will be an offence if a Town Council, without reasonable excuse, persistently fails to submit its financial statements on time.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Clauses 23 and 31 expand the scope of rules that MND can prescribe and Town Councils must comply in the areas of finance and governance.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: These include rules for Town Councils to disclose their compliance with governance standards.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: MND will work with Town Councils to finetune these reporting instruments and roll them out in due course.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: In particular, we will work with Town Councils to develop a Code of Governance for Town Councils.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This will take reference from similar Codes for Charities and Companies, which seek to strengthen accountability and boost public confidence in the respective sectors.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The Code will cover best practices that Town Councils are encouraged to adopt through a comply-or-explain regime.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Besides strengthening disclosure requirements, the Bill also seeks to strengthen internal controls in relation to potential conflicts of interest within a Town Council and related parties.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Clauses 8, 13 and 16 disqualify the Town Council's Managing Agent (MA) and its appointed auditor from concurrently holding key roles in a Town Council, at the Town Council, Town Councils' committee and executive levels.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: These roles pose a conflict of interest risk because the Auditor is tasked to conduct an independent and objective assessment of the Town Councils' finances.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The MA provides a significant proportion of Town Councils' services and could stand to gain from how contracts are awarded by the Town Council.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We have intentionally nuanced these prohibitions, as disqualification is a heavy bar.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: It is certainly not our intention to stop individuals with the relevant skillsets and experience, for example, in audit and estate management, from serving residents in the Town Councils.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The scenario that we want to avoid is one where a person wields significant influence or power in two conflicting roles, for example, as General Manager of the Town Council and the Chief Executive Officer or Managing Partner in the Town Council's MA.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Non-C-suite executives and other regular employees of the Auditor and MA are not barred from double-hatting in the Town Council.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Nevertheless, we will require, in clause 9, Town Council staff to make disclosure of interests to the Town Council and to recuse themselves from decision-making if there is potential conflict.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Next, I will move on to enhancements in the Bill that aim to strengthen the way Town Councils manage their finances.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Earlier this year, we announced a series of steps that MND will take to ensure that Town Councils take a long-term view of their finances and start setting aside monies for big ticket items, such as lift and other asset replacements.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The provisions in the Bill give legislative effect to some of these measures.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The detailed mechanics of LRF, such as the minimum contribution rates, will be set out in the subsidiary legislation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: As announced earlier, additional grants will also be provided to help Town Councils accumulate sufficient funds.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Second, the Bill empowers MND to make rules for Town Councils to prepare and maintain long-term financial plans.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Clause 23 will instil greater financial discipline among Town Councils to review their financial positions regularly and to make timely adjustments to their financial plans in response to changes in the operating environment.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Third, the Bill introduces safeguards that avoid service disruptions, if a Town Council is on the brink of financial insolvency.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Clause 23 allows MND to make rules under the TCFR that prescribe Town Councils' course of action in such scenarios.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This could include the appointment of advisors to advise the Town Council on the proper management of its affairs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Under the current Town Councils Act, MND's regulatory levers to secure compliance from Town Councils with the law are limited.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: While MND is responsible for administering the Act, it lacks powers to require Town Councils to submit any information beyond their annual financial statements.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: In addition, MND lacks the regulatory levers to intervene where there is a detected non-compliance with the Act.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: There are only three narrow areas where non-compliance with the Act is now an offence: one, the misuse of Town Council funds; two, the contravention of Lift Upgrading Programme Rules; and three, the failure to provide information to the auditor without reasonable excuse.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: First, in addition to the annual financial reporting, MND may periodically conduct compliance reviews to check for regulatory compliance.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: These are basically health checks, in the form of risk-based audits on different aspects of Town Councils' operations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The objective is to assess if there are specific areas of non-compliance, process gaps or areas for improvement.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: MND will appoint inspectors, who may be public officers or professionals with the relevant qualifications and experience, to conduct these reviews.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: During these reviews, Town Councillors and staff will have to answer queries from the inspectors and produce documents upon request.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: At the end of the review, the inspectors' findings and recommendations for improvement will be presented to both MND and the Town Council.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Town Councillors and Town Council staff will be expected to extend their full cooperation to the inspectors during the investigation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This rectification order will specify remedial actions for the Town Council to address the irregularity and a timeframe to do so.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: At the end of the specified period, the Town Council is to report on the action it has taken.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: To be very clear, this provision of last resort is not new and is already present in the current Town Councils Act.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The Bill merely repeals the provision under section 50 and reintroduces it in the new section 43G.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The various steps that I have just outlined enable MND to take timely action and calibrate its enforcement approach according to the action, or inaction, of the Town Council.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: In practical implementation, MND will first seek to engage the Town Councils to understand the situation and determine the severity of any contravention.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Town Councils will continue to be responsible for correcting any lapses or management deficiencies that are uncovered in the course of the compliance reviews and investigations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: As I have said earlier, the findings by the inspectors will be shared with both MND and the Town Council.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: While the Bill has introduced stronger enforcement powers to investigate and require Town Councils to take specific remedial actions, they will generally be exercised when a Town Council is uncooperative or recalcitrant, refusing to correct irregularities despite due and fair notice.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The Bill will make it an offence when Town Councils fail to provide regular submissions relating to audit and governance or fail to cooperate with requests for information relating to governance.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Town Councils can be taken to task for flouting financial rules or specific instructions to rectify their contraventions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Three, abiding by public laws and cooperating with public authorities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Town Councils can be taken to task for making unlawful collections or putting public health and safety at risk.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Where applicable, we have benchmarked the penalties to those for similar offences under the Charities Act.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We all recognise and accept that Town Councils and their key decision-makers have to act honestly and responsibly.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This is reflected in section 33(6B) of the current Town Councils Act where key decision-makers in the Town Council, namely, the Chairman and Secretary, are held equally liable for the offence committed by the Town Council, if the offence was committed with their consent or connivance.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The Bill extends this existing treatment and penalties to the new offence provisions, so as to hold culpable parties accountable.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This sets the tone for the leadership of Town Councils and underscores the point that there would be stern consequences for key decision-makers who abet poor governance or fail in their fiduciary duties.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: To streamline the enforcement process, clause 26 will also empower MND to offer composition for some of the offences.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This will enable MND to take mitigating or aggravating factors into consideration when deciding whether to compound an offence or proceed to recommend prosecution to the public prosecutor.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Besides what I have covered above, the Bill includes amendments to clarify existing definitions and processes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: It also covers Town Council handover processes which have been a subject of review, and a handover guide in 2013.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: These amendments have adhered to the original spirit and intent of allowing Town Councils to operate autonomously, while establishing the necessary standards of governance, public accountability and transparency that residents and the general public expect of our Town Councils, standards that this Parliament voted for in February 2015 to strengthen through legislation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: With a stronger regulatory framework, MND will play a more effective role to safeguard residents' interests and public funds.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We hope that these amendments can give residents greater assurance that their housing estates are properly managed and S&CC monies are used for their benefit.

speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
text: As elected MPs running Town Councils, we owe a duty of care to our residents and the public to manage our HDB estates properly and in compliance with the Town Councils Act and financial rules.

speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
text: We must also ensure that Town Councils get value for money when procuring products and services.

speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
text: This includes providing fair and open competition, proper tender evaluation and awarding contracts to ensure public accountability.

speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
text: Against this backdrop, the 15 PAP Town Councils support the amendments which will guide all Town Councils to better serve our residents.

speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
text: While MND has so far adopted a light-touch approach as regulator, I appreciate that a "light-touch" does not mean "no touch".

speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
text: Recent events have also shown us that not all Town Councils act decisively to rectify problems that surface.

speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
text: At the end of the day, MND must be given the powers to move in and nip the problems in the bud and ensure that public interest is not compromised.

speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
text: We look forward to working with MND to identify ways in which we can continue to improve to serve our residents better.

speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
text: This arrangement enables elected MPs to manage and serve their residents and, more importantly, ensures that they are accountable to their residents when running the estates.

speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
text: Over the past 28 years, many elected PAP MPs have run Town Councils to serve their residents.

speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
text: These PAP Town Councils have always practised financial prudence to ensure that they provide quality maintenance services to their residents.

speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
text: The PAP Town Councils have also been diligently submitting their audited accounts, financial statements and annual reports on time to Parliament for the purposes of public accountability.

speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
text: This requirement is necessary as it will ensure that all Town Councils will not only keep proper records of their accounts, but also have their accounts properly audited by independent auditors.

speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
text: This results in greater transparency and will allow Town Councils greater accountability to their residents.

speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
text: In this regard, I propose that the Ministry set down rules pertaining to the format and presentation of the audited accounts and financial statements, so as to facilitate greater understanding of the accounts by the residents.

speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
text: In such instances, most Town Councils follow the handing and taking over guidelines provided by MND to effect the handover.

speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
text: Generally, most Town Councils have not encountered any major problems when taking over the property data, financial data, contracts and work in progress from the previous staff in the Town Councils who were managing the information.

speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
text: Moreover, the Town Councils which are taking over would usually set up their own computer systems to manage both their accounts and estates in order to serve their residents better.

speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
text: However, in order to enhance the effectiveness of this clause, I would urge the Ministry to lay out clear rules and procedures for Town Councils to comply with.

speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
text: This would include rules and procedures for the listing of property database, customer information, assets and liabilities, ongoing contracts and work in progress.

speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
text: In the interest of fairness, the Ministry can also appoint an independent auditor to oversee both the handing and taking over of all Town Councils.

speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
text: Further, in the event of a dispute amongst the Town Councils, the Ministry can mediate or arbitrate the conflict and propose an amicable solution that will better serve the interests of the residents.

speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
text: Although HDB has developed a comprehensive management system to ensure the quality of new flats, building defects are still commonly found in flats that HDB hands over to the Town Councils.

speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
text: Common defects include frequent lift breakdowns, water leakages and seepages, wall and ceiling plaster cracks, and incomplete external site works.

speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
text: Most of these defects can often be attributed to either poor or impractical designs, or shoddy workmanship during construction.

speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
text: Town Councils frequently experience great difficulty in getting the relevant consultants and contractors to rectify the defects properly and promptly due to their lack of authority over them.

speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
text: As a result, this has caused much anxiety and unhappiness amongst flat owners, MPs and Town Council staff.

speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
text: In this way, HDB will be directly responsible in ensuring the quality of both the design and construction of new flats which satisfy the needs of the flat owners before these flats are handed over to the Town Councils for management.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: We are debating this Bill with a view to improve the existing Act.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: I do not oppose the objective per se but, as an Opposition MP, my experience is that Town Councils operate quite differently by design in PAP and Opposition wards and, as such, are inevitably judged by different yardsticks.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: We believe an independent entity of inspectors, not appointed by the Government, should resolve disputes if and when they occur between MND and the affected Town Council, a point that Ms Sylvia Lim will build upon.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: The additional scrutiny on Town Councils is not objectionable.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: It is the identity of the scrutiniser that warrants scrutiny.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: According to then Deputy Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong, there were two philosophical objectives behind the original Town Councils Act.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: It gives the MPs and residents greater power and responsibility to manage their own affairs and to participate in the estate's development.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: However, the transfer of power from HDB to the MPs and, I stress, grassroots leaders, is only partial in an Opposition Town Council as the grassroots are, by design, not part of the Opposition Town Council's firmament.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: This is because the Government cannot reconcile that an Opposition MP and, by extension, an Opposition Town Council, would support the Government's plans.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: It is also instructive that nowhere does the grassroots, Community Improvement Projects Committee (CIPC) or the People's Association appear in the Town Councils Act.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Yet, the grassroots were acknowledged as a conspicuous and central part of the Town Council system when the Bill was debated in 1988.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: This is because the Town Councils Act was legislated to serve a dominant one-party state and, to that end, Government-sanctioned grassroots organisations do not work with elected MPs in Opposition Town Councils.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: This remains a fundamental omission vis-a-vis the operation of Town Councils in Opposition wards.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: I have spoken on how the grassroots have a significant say on estate upgrading via CIPC funding in this House previously and I do not repeat those points here.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: The same can be said about the political control of critical Town Council management systems and software by politically influenced entities.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: One can just compare the amount of state resources extended via the CIPC committee through the grassroots in PAP Town Councils compared to Opposition Town Councils.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Certainly, lesser taxpayer funds to Town Councils will inevitably lower the esteem of Opposition-run Town Councils with attendant political ramifications.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: While I believe this should change and a fairer system ought to take form, as a political realist, I can see why the ruling party will rather institutionalise the status quo.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: In view of some fundamental disparities between the Opposition and PAP Town Councils in practice, WP would have approached this amendment Bill with the words of the then Deputy Prime Minister Mr S Dhanabalan in his round-up speech on the original Town Council Bill some 30 years ago.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: He said, "The question really is not better or not there is a political purpose.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: The question is: is the purpose a good one for Singapore?

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Will it make for a more stable and secure Singapore?

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Will it make for a better life for our citizens?

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: That is the question we ought to ask." I would like to state for the record that WP is under no illusion that the purpose of the Town Councils Act is undeniably political.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: And since 1988, PAP politicians have come up openly to say so.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: But the former Deputy Prime Minister's subsequent questions remain relevant today.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: This will not necessarily ensure good outcomes for Singapore but rather politically good outcomes for any ruling party.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Central to the working of the Town Councils are the powers of the elected MPs in relation to MND.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Critical to the success of the Town councils is the protection of the MPs' autonomy, guaranteed as a political space for the MPs to work with local residents so that the same residents voting in the General Election can judge the MPs' performance.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: If we return to the speech of the then Deputy Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong during the 1988 debate, he raised three important points.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: First, it was not the original intention that HDB become the management corporation for 80% of the population.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Second, when our people become too dependent on HDB, it will lose self-reliance and its responsibility for their own surroundings.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: In a sense, they will expect HDB to fix and do everything.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: If citizens know that MND will intervene when the town is not run effectively, then whether the candidates standing for election are honest and effective enough to run the Town Council potentially becomes irrelevant.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: As envisaged by the Town Councils Act originally, voters are responsible for the MPs they choose to run their towns and represent them in Parliament.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: If they do not like what they see, they can vote under-performing MPs out at the next elections.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: MND having oversight over the Town Council does not mean just over-centralisation potentially but it also leads the two political pervasions.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: I would suggest to this House that there is a better way to move forward on this point while retaining the proposed oversight powers sought by this Bill that will, at the same time, preserve the central feature of Town Councils – the political autonomy of MPs.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Those oversight powers should be in the hands of independent parties not linked to the Ministry or the Government in general.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: This is critical to preserving the Town Councils as a ballast to our democracy.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: I would take the point made by hon Member Dr Teo Ho Pin about the potential of introducing an independent auditor during the time when an estate is handed over, especially between political parties.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: In fact, the same call was made more recently in the public consultation on this Bill.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: It would be helpful if the Government looked into why many Singaporeans, or at least the polled Singaporeans, are not as enthusiastic about Town Councils in spite of its objectives, not all of which are necessarily objectionable.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: I do think there is much value in getting MPs involved in local politics and the nitty-gritty of constituency work.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: In spite of the different realities on the ground and the treatment between Opposition and PAP Town Councils, particularly as a result of the grassroots and, by extension, losing PAP political candidates to the People's Association, WP is determined to make the best of less than an equitable situation, managing it not with the cards we wish we had, but those that are in our hands.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Can he explain what his proposal is, so that I can better understand it?

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: That is what the poll said, but can I understand in this House what is his position and what is the position of WP in respect of the position of Town Councils in our elected system?

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: It is not the position that the poll suggested.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: What the poll is telling us is that the public may have a different view about it and that is something for MND to consider.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: Because it is working in the current context as the Senior Minister of State would know in the case of Aljunied-Hougang Town Council.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: The key point is that if there is an independent individual, I think that will be a better position or better outcome for Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: On his second point, he said that if the auditor or the inspector is an independent inspector, he would support Part VI A.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: Senior Minister of State, I would suggest that it would, provided you can provide us with more details on how those independent investigators would be appointed.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: As a Town Council chairman who has had to hand over a constituency to another Town Council in 2013 and then take it back again in 2015, I can understand very well the need to have some of these amendments.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: After the by-election in 2013, Punggol East was handed over to the Aljunied-Hougang Town Council (AHTC).

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: AHTC gave PRPGTC three different sets of audited financial statements on three different dates.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: AHTC withdrew the first and second sets on 26 January 2017, when PRPGTC perhaps identified some discrepancies in the first audited statements.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: PRPGTC is looking through this third set carefully and we have already identified several discrepancies.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: First, could the Minister consider setting a reasonable deadline for the preparation and submission of audited financial statements on the distribution of assets and liabilities if section 38(11) does not apply to the audited financial statements on the distribution of assets and liabilities?

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Second, PRPGTC could have submitted our audited financial statements on the distribution of assets and liabilities earlier if both Town Councils could have agreed in writing on the allocation method to be used to distribute the assets and liabilities as required by our own auditors.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Hence, I would like the Minister to consider including in the Bill the allocation method to be used to determine the distribution of assets and liabilities or, alternatively, for the Bill to allow the Minister to determine the method to be used during the handover process.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Another area that I would like the Minister to consider is allowing a Town Council to maintain two separate financial accounts pending the submission of an unqualified audited financial statements of a constituency the Town Council is taking over.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: PRPGTC has had an excellent record where our annual financial statements were all unqualified.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: To meet MND's statutory requirement for the submission of annual audited financial statements in August 2016, PRPTC had included Punggol East Single Member Constituency's (SMC's) unaudited financial statements into the PRPTC's FY2015/2016 audited financial statements.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Our earlier request to maintain two separate accounts was denied by MND.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: It was unfortunate that the poor practices and failure of compliance by the outgoing Town Council then "contaminated" the entire set of accounts for the whole of PRPGTC, through no fault of our own.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: The submission of audited financial statements is a standard practice and part and parcel of ensuring good governance.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: If a Town Council maintains good and proper Town Council record, it is a straightforward process.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: But if the appointed auditors are unable to verify the accounts due to lack of information, it is usually an early sign of poor financial and corporate governance.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: I also am heartened to note that the Town Councils Act, section 3, has been amended to address the boundary change.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: The new amendment under section 3(3A)(e) requires the outgoing Town Council to provide another Town Council with all documents, information and other assistance as the Town Council may reasonably require to manage the area and serve the residents.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: In our experience, despite the assurance of cooperation from the outgoing Town Council management, PRPGTC faced a lot of challenges to be operationally ready by 1 December 2015 to serve Punggol East due to the lack of documents and insufficient information provided to us.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: This directly affected our ability to serve the residents and had caused inconvenience to many households.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Operational difficulties faced by PRPGTC included being unable to share with residents the breakdown of S&CC arrears owing to the Town Council because AHTC's record only showed a lumpsum owed without showing a detailed monthly breakdown of the payment arrears.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: PRPGTC also had to manage cases of residents accumulating arrears because they were not informed by AHPETC prior to 1 December 2015 that their general interbank recurring orders (GIRO) arrangements had been stopped.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: All of this essential information was not shared and affected the residents.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: As such, with reference to section 3(3A)(e), I would like to ask the Minister if the incoming Town Council can apply to the Minister to instruct the outgoing Town Council to provide more data or information as required by the incoming Town Council.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: This is important because the lack of complete documents and information can hamper the ability of the incoming Town Council to serve and thereby causing much inconvenience to the residents.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: I also support the amendments in the Bill to improve MND's regulatory oversight to ensure Town Councils comply with the Act and Rules.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: All Town Councils manage a substantial amount of money, and non-compliance by Town Councils can have repercussions downstream.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Hence, it would be prudent to ensure MND has regulatory oversight.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: One of the regulatory issues where compliance is required by a Town Council is to ensure quarterly transfers of the S&CC fees collected into the sinking fund.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Failure to perform this quarterly transfer could imply two things.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: First, the Town Council is not doing their job well to manage their accounts; or second, the Town Council has overspent on routine maintenance and, hence, do not have sufficient funds to make the required sinking fund transfer.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: If MND has greater oversight, such a Town Council should be brought to task to observe the regulatory requirement and this will ensure that any regulatory non-compliance problem is detected early and solved before it escalates into a huge mess.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: On the topic of accountability, the current Town Councils Act only holds two positions responsible, the Chairman and Secretary, for any cases of criminal liability.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: I support this amendment because Town Council operations do require some decision-making to be done by various key officers or Town Councillors.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: As such, this amendment would ensure the key officers could be held accountable for their decision-making.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: The KPMG report on AHTC illustrates the need for this amendment where several problems were uncovered.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: The Nanyang Technological University's (NTU's) accounting professor El'fred Boo was quoted during an interview with Channel NewsAsia (CNA) that the findings have, I quote, "serious and grave implications for the parties involved in the AHTC scandal, including a potential basis for filing criminal charges if a deliberate intent could be established".

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: This was corroborated by instances of overpayments, and payments without approval and certification of work performed".

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: The involvement of many individuals appointed by the Town Council illustrates the need why they need to be held accountable, other than the Chairman or Secretary, if criminal intent can be established.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: In addition, these amendments would ensure that any inconvenience to residents would be minimised following changes to a Town Council after a General Election.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: The amendments would ensure that the key Town Council personnel will be held accountable if there is evidence of criminal intent in their decision-making while managing Town Council affairs.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: Yes, I will start off my clarifications before Mr Singh does.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: He was going on about the handover of Punggol East and saying that Pasir Ris/Punggol East Town Council had a lot of operational problems and so on.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: But I am quite surprised to hear that because can he not confirm that AHTC and PRPGTC have actually met many times for the handover and has he ever raised these problems to our Chairman?

speaker: Mdm Speaker
text: Ms Lim, can you please address your comments to me?

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: The second clarification is that the Member talked about late transfers of sinking funds and his observation was that it could only mean that we have overspent our routine funds and so on.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: But does he not agree that if a Town Council is deprived of Government grants, that could also be a reason why it may not be able to make timely sinking fund transfers?

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: The third point is that the Member quoted a professor talking about the KPMG past payment review where the professor mentioned that there could be some criminal liability involved.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari
text: On the issue whether we have met several times to resolve some of these operational issues, yes, I think we have met several times.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari
text: But during many of these meetings, while there is assurance of cooperation, our Town Council faced a lot of challenges.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari
text: On the second point, with regard to the late transfer of sinking funds, I did not make any specific reference to any Town Council.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari
text: Then, on the third point about the quote that I cited from Prof El'fred Boo of criminal liability, I have read actually the report by KPMG.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari
text: As to whether there is criminal liability, it is not for me to establish whether there is criminal intent.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: My question is very simple − whether there was any finding that there is criminal intent.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: Can I just ask Mr Zainal Sapari, Ms Sylvia Lim asked him a question when there were these alleged difficulties that he mentioned at the operational level, did he write to, at least, the Chairman, myself or the vice-chairman of the Town Council what those problems were, so that we could help him resolve them?

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: Because my understanding was we actually tried to work as best as we can in the circumstances that we were in to ensure a smooth handover.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: With regard to the earlier comment made about some delay in handover of financial statements, eight and a half months and so forth, can I just ask the Member Mr Zainal Sapari when Punggol East was transferred to AHPETC after the 2013 Elections, when was the last instalment of sinking funds made by PRPGTC to AHTC?

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: And how does that compare with the final instalment that was made to PRPGTC, as has been reported in the media today, I believe?

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari
text: With regard to the first clarification whether we had engaged the Chairman of the Town Council, these are all done by the Secretariat, by the Town Council staff, to actually work directly with the staff from AHTC.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari
text: What was shared with me was information that was told to me by my staff.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari
text: The subsequent amount was eventually transferred to AHTC after we have resolved all the accounts.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: With regard to the reply to the first question, the point remains that it was open to Mr Zainal Sapari to write to me and he chose not to.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: On the second point, I believe that the final transfer of the sinking funds or outstanding funds to AHTC was made in September 2014, some one-and-a-half years after the by-election in Punggol East SMC.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: I believe the deadline is not too different from the final transfer or final instalment made by AHTC to PRPGTC.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: He has read the report, that is what he said.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: Was there a finding in the report that there was criminal intent?

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: Number two, since he has read the report, if there is no such finding, what is his view?

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari
text: With regard to the second question, what is my view, that is the whole purpose of having this amendment − it is to make sure that we improve on our financial governance.

speaker: Mdm Speaker
text: Can I advise Members to address the Chair and not to talk to each other?

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: We actually engaged the same contractor that did the transfer from Potong Pasir Town Council to the PAP Town Council.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: It is the same contractor and there is no issue raised.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: Actually, along the way, we keep asking the contractor any major issues, but there were no issues raised.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: So, this is the first time that I am hearing this.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: So, maybe the Member can explain what are these issues with the data transfer?

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari
text: We could always share later on with AHTC, if it so desires, what were some of the information given to us and they were not complete for us to be operationally-ready.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This is the Second Reading, the purpose of which is to debate the principles behind the Bill.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: I understand that Mr Zainal Sapari had raised this as an example of certain concerns that he hopes the Bill will address.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: I also understand the Members from WP have got different points of view, and I think that has been registered.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We will just seek Madam's leave to allow the principles of this Bill to continue to be debated as part of Second Reading.

speaker: Mdm Speaker
text: I agree entirely with the Senior Minister of State Desmond Lee.

speaker: Mdm Speaker
text: We are debating about the general principles of the Bill.

speaker: Mdm Speaker
text: Can Ms Sylvia Lim please proceed with your speech?

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: And in doing so, I will draw on my experience as the former Chairman of AHPETC and as the current Vice-Chairman of AHTC.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: A key feature of this Bill is on conflicts of interest, as provided in clauses 8, 9, 10 and 13.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: First, let me say that WP agrees that conflicts of interest should be managed carefully.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: This certainly applies to Town Councils which handle tens of millions of dollars of public funds each year by way of S&CC payments from residents and Government grants.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: The Bill recognises that conflicts of interest will arise from time to time and need to be managed.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: Indeed, the practice of declaring potential conflicts of interest and recusing oneself from decision-making is unobjectionable and has been in place in our Town Council since inception.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: The Bill focuses on the potential conflicts that can arise where a Town Council appoints an MA to manage the Town.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: The post of Town Council Secretary/General Manager (GM), is an onerous one involving both compliance with regulations and leadership of a large operation.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: Where town management is outsourced to an MA, the person appointed to assume the heavy duties of Secretary or GM will not be a junior staff from the MA.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: In fact, we know that prior to General Election 2011, Aljunied Town Council was managed by an MA where the Town Council Secretary/GM was the Managing Director of the MA.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: So, conflicts of potential conflicts exist in PAP Town Councils as well.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: Earlier in his Second Reading Speech, Senior Minister of State Desmond Lee mentioned that it would catch officers in the C-suite.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: But as it is phrased, it is about people having significant influence.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: I would argue that it is likely to be larger than the C-suite.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: So, I think the Ministry should clarify this point.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: The proposed section 15(2) will require the Town Council Secretary to maintain a Register of Declarations of interests and potential conflicts of interest made by Town Councillors.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: This Register of Interest of Declarations is to be kept and maintained by the Town Council Secretary, and each disclosure is to be brought up at the relevant Town Council meetings.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: In our view, this is useful but does not go far enough.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: Instead of just maintaining the Register, we would call for all such registers to be published for the scrutiny of residents.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: On our part, we are ready to publish the declarations related to AHTC.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: Next, I move on to the proposed mechanism for oversight.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: I now turn to clause 24 which introduces a new Part VIA on Oversight and Monitoring of Town Councils.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: These new provisions give the Minister powers that he did not have before.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: The Courts analysed that the framework of the Town Councils Act clearly showed that the Minister was only entitled to intervene in very few and specific circumstances and did not have a general power of oversight.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: Insofar as this Bill purports to enable the Ministry to manage or even curtail a Town Council's work, this goes against the original intent of forming Town Councils in the first place.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: He may also order such an investigation if a Town Council under a compliance review does not produce certain information required by the review.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: First, I would like to point out that there is already an existing framework in place.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: As it stands, Town Councils undergo annual audits, and auditors flag out issues on an annual basis.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: Where there is concern about a particular Town Council, the Auditor-General's Office (AGO) can be called in, just as the Government did to AHPETC in 2014.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: The AGO team would devote time and expertise to unravel any matters and issue public reports.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: Matters can also be referred to law enforcement agencies, if warranted, as with the case of the Ang Mo Kio Town Council's GM being referred to the Corrupt Practices Investigation Bureau (CPIB).

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: So, why the extreme step of giving the Minister investigative powers over Town Councils?

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: Furthermore, what amounts to "a reasonable suspicion of a material irregularity" is very subjective.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: The Bill does not even require any irregularity to be proved, just a suspicion of a material irregularity.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: What would trigger such an investigation is purely up to the Minister to interpret.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: But the Minister himself is supposed to be running a Town Council, too, as are his Senior Minister of State and Minister of State.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: His bosses, the Prime Minister, the Deputy Prime Ministers and the Coordinating Minister for Infrastructure, are all also running Town Councils.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: Their comrades in arms are running all the Town Councils in Singapore except one − our WP Town Council.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: Is the Minister a suitable gatekeeper, with these massive conflicts of interest?

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: It is not possible to argue that the Ministry is a politically neutral body, as recent history, unfortunately, belies that claim.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: Singaporeans will recall that during the General Election campaign in 2015, the Ministry was an active campaigner against WP, issuing statements practically daily on the alleged misconduct of AHPETC.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: After Polling Day, the Ministry took a break and little was heard for weeks.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: To take another example: we have also seen past records of how the Ministry advised a PAP Town Council how to make good a breach of TCFRs quietly behind closed doors, without any media release on the same.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: These are but two examples of the double standards practised by the current Government.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: It is, in our view, dangerous to arrogate to a partisan Minister the solemn duty of overseeing Town Councils, which are essentially political institutions.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: Furthermore, according to the new section 43E, the persons the Minister will appoint as inspectors of Town Councils include public servants and HDB employees.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: These civil servants depend on their jobs to support their families.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: Do we expect these HDB officers to issue stinging reports against the Town Councils run by the Prime Minister or the Minister for National Development?

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: If they do, they should be ready to throw in their resignations.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: From the corporate governance standpoint, experts have noted that having Town Councils report to MND is problematic.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: For instance, it was observed by Assoc Prof Mak Yuen Teen that the current model had MPs as Town Councillors responsible for Town Councils that are overseen by MND.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: But MND was also accountable to the same people who are Ministers or MPs.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: He said, "I think this creates, at least, perception issues… that the system might be unfair or lenient to Town Councils because the PAP dominates the Government".

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: We reject this scheme as being fundamentally flawed.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: Having said that, Madam, we have two suggestions on how the public interest may be safeguarded in the context of Town Councils.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: First, while we cannot accept what is proposed in Part VIA, we totally support the principle that Town Councils should be subject to regular audits and checks due to the significant amounts of public funds they manage.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: It fiercely defends its independence and has earned a good reputation for highlighting problems in Government departments and Statutory Boards.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: Such a scheme of AGO audits would engender greater confidence that the exercise is impartial and focus on what the public interest is, safeguarding of public monies.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: Our second suggestion involves the resolution of disputes or differences between MND, HDB and other Government agencies on the one hand, and Town Councils and residents on the other hand.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: The new section 21A will require Town Councils to work cooperatively and collaboratively with HDB, NEA and others.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: There seems to be a presumption in the Bill that the Government agency is always right, that Town Councils have no legitimate case, and Town Councils should simply comply with what HDB or NEA tell them to do.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: Town Councils will be liable to fines if there is non-compliance.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: I will just give three examples to illustrate.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: For instance, HDB may wish to erect structures which will become a burden for the Town Councils to maintain; or Government agencies may require information from Town Councils in certain prescribed formats, which non-PAP Town Councils will incur significant time and cost to produce; or HDB may take a hands-off approach when Town Councils or residents face problems with the Design, Build and Sell Scheme (DBSS) flats, resulting in slow resolution or non-resolution of issues by the developer.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: It may be natural for HDB to defend its own interest but that does not equate to the public interest.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: Currently, the dispute resolution mechanism between Government agencies, Town Councils and residents is the Courts.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: This is not ideal as Court processes are time-consuming and costly to Town Councils and residents.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: Going to Court is also adversarial in nature and would jeopardise the relationship between the Government, the Town Council and residents.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: The tribunal should be chaired by a Judge and have members who are qualified in relevant fields, such as engineering, architecture, project management and horticulture.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: The tribunal could function with procedures which are low-cost and less formal.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: The setting up of such a tribunal would go a long way towards having a more considered and just resolution of disputes, and residents will automatically benefit.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: According to the Town Councils Act, the role of the Town Council is to control, manage, maintain and improve the common property of the residential and commercial property in an HDB estate.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: On the ground, the actual work of the Town Council is very wide-ranging.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: For example, it is the Town Council that ensures that the common areas of the HDB estates are cleaned, that rubbish is cleared from rubbish bins, that rubbish chutes are flushed regularly, that the lights at the common corridors, void decks, car parks and other common areas are properly maintained, that the lifts are maintained and repaired whenever they break down.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: In addition to the daily maintenance work of the HDB estate, the Town Council also carries out cyclical works like major repainting works, renewal and replacement of roofing system, replacement of water tanks, pumps and water supply system, fire-fighting and protection systems, water pipes and water pump sets and lifts.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: These cyclical works involve huge expenses as the scope of the work is much larger.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Many Town Councils also carry out improvement projects like installing children's playgrounds, fitness corners and building covered linkways.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: The revenue of the Town Council comes mainly from S&CC collected from residents and from Government grants.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: From the S&CC collected, Town Councils will have to set aside a proportion of its revenue to a sinking fund to cater to the future expenses for its cyclical works.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Most Town Councils would need to set aside millions of dollars in its sinking funds because such cyclical works involve huge capital expenses.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: The Town Council needs to ensure that they have enough funds in its sinking funds to cater for future cyclical expenses as and when they are required.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: I served 16 years in the Legal and Finance committee of Jalan Besar Town Council and then moved on to serve in the Marine Parade Town Council from 2006 to today.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Over these past years, a large part of my time doing Town Council-related matters is spent on reviewing contract awards.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: It is critical to ensure that contracts awarded by the Town Council are all done above board and that commercial decisions by the Town Council are made without any self-interest involved.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Many of the contracts awarded by Town Councils to their contractors are of high value and in the hundreds of thousands of dollars.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: So, these are large sums of money involved.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Because of the large sums of moneys involved and given the fact that the Town Council handles funds collected from the public, I support any rules to tighten financial management and to introduce rules of governance.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: I wish to touch briefly on four points in the Bill.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: First, clause 9 talks about conflict of interest and disclosures.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: The requirement to disclose conflicts of interest at clause 9 is nothing new.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: It is already in section 15 of the existing Act.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: In many charities and voluntary welfare organisations (VWOs), similar requirements on disclosures are also imposed.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: What is fundamental to every organisation dealing with the award of contracts is the need to keep the system transparent and to have good governance.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Otherwise, if a Town Council member with a business interest in a major project does not declare his interest, he may then be able to persuade members within the same committee to award a contract to him at an inflated price.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: In such a case, there is likelihood of abuse of the system.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: At the end of the day, the interest of the residents would suffer as the Town Council may be paying above market prices to its contractor who has a vested interest in serving in the Town Council.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: It also begs the question as to who is looking after the interest of the residents if there is conflict of interest.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: I also support the amendment to extend the conflict of interest disclosure requirements to the Secretary, an employee, a staff or MA of the Town Council.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Senior staff members of the Town Council sometimes do have influence over members of the Council because of friendship built up over the years.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: These staff members should also be required to disclose their interest in any contracts to be awarded by the Town Council to their company or to their associates.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Otherwise, it would be easy for staff members to persuade Town Council members that the best contractor in any tender is their own company in which they have a vested interest.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Given that the Town Council awards contracts of large values regularly, it would be easy for someone with a vested interest to benefit from these contracts.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: This is a common requirement for many Accounting and Corporate Regulatory Authority (ACRA)-registered companies.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: I was surprised that this six-month deadline was not a previous requirement.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Next point, clause 14, interaction between Town Councils and statutory authorities.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: I understand the intent behind the clause is to ensure that Town Councils do not impede the work of a statutory body for the purposes stated at section 21A, that is, to secure public safety, ensure public order, prevent disease or injury or create and maintain a healthy environment.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
