text: These are all clearly meant for the benefit of the residents of the HDB estate and to improve their quality of life.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: However, I wish to raise an issue which the Town Council faces on the ground.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: To cite an example, Town Council issues summonses or notices to shopkeepers to keep the common area free of clutter.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: The shopkeeper may choose to pay the fine.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Then, when a statutory body like the Singapore Civil Defence Force (SCDF) inspects the place, they ignore the fact that the Town Council has been trying to enforce the regulations.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: They ignore the fact that the Town Council does not have power to take injunctions against a recalcitrant shopkeeper.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Instead, SCDF issues a summons to the Town Council for failure to comply with safety regulations.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Is there a better way in which the Town Council can work with HDB or statutory bodies to address such issues?

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: If a Town Council is fully cooperative and wishes to ensure that there is compliance with the regulations imposed by the Government, can the Government agency consider that Town Council's efforts and attempts in getting the residents or shopkeepers to comply with the law?

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: You see, even PAP Town Councils are not immune from the arms of the Government agencies.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: And each Town Council is required to set aside part of its sinking funds for the lift replacement fund.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: In Marine Parade, there are about 1,400 lifts.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: In some of the bigger towns, like Ang Mo Kio, there are more than 2,000 lifts.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Each lift would have an operational lifespan after which the Town Council would eventually have to replace the lift.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Thus, for older estates, if the flats are more than 30 years old, the lifts are likely to be 30 years old and prone to frequent breakdowns due to its mechanical age.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Setting aside a lift replacement fund is a prudent and responsible thing to do.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Otherwise, years from now, when the time comes to replace these lifts because they are no longer serviceable, then it is foreseeable that the Town Council may not have sufficient funds to pay for the replacement costs of all the lifts.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: In some private estates, if a situation like this happens, the residents would be forced to pay a special capital levy of a large sum of money to pay for the lift replacement.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: The alternative is for the residents to do without the lift.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Thus, it is financially prudent that the Town Council set aside part of its sinking fund collection now to ensure that the Town Council does not have to suddenly raise funds to pay for a large bill when the time comes to pay for the lift replacement.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: It would be irresponsible for any Town Council to kick the can down the road and leave it to future residents to solve the problem of raising funds to pay for lift replacement.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: When the Bill was tabled, one of the things that caused me some concern was clause 25 of the Bill.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Thus, if a Town Council had committed an offence under section 21A(4) or section 43D(4) of the Town Councils Act, not only would the Town Council be subject to a fine, the Chairman or Secretary of the Town Council would also be guilty of the same offence if the provisions of section 48A(1)(b) are met.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: The clause does seem onerous for the Chairman and the Secretary as it involves personal liability for the two office bearers.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: If found guilty, the Chairman or the Secretary would be liable to a fine or to imprisonment.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: I agree that if a Chairman or Secretary had consented or connived to effect the commission of an offence, or if that person had, by act or omission, knowingly been concerned in or is a party to the commission of an offence by the Town Council, then some degree of penalty on a personal basis is warranted.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: However, sub paragraph (iii) of section 48A(1) seems to place a heavier burden on that person.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: And in some circumstances, it is really not so easy to determine whether a person knew or ought reasonably to have known that the offence by the Town Council would be committed.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Can the Senior Minister of State clarify under what circumstances would this clause be invoked?

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Before I close, Mdm Speaker, allow me to comment on some of the views expressed earlier by hon Members of the House.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: As far as I can recall, Hougang Town Council has been in existence for many years.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: What I know is that Mr Low Thia Khiang had managed his Town Council well for many years.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: He gathered his own group of supporters and he was elected again and again.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: It is for this reason we have clause 24 or Part VIA of this Bill.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: It is good and for the benefit of the residents and, therefore, I support the Bill.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
text: I wish to thank Mr Lim Biow Chuan for his comment on Hougang Town Council (HTC).

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
text: I would say that even today, if you look at the management of a Town Council, whether it is AHPETC or HTC, we manage the Town Council relatively well, if you look at the Town Council Management Report of HDB.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
text: We lacked the financial accounting system that is able to cope and manage a large Group Representation Constituency (GRC) —

speaker: Mdm Speaker
text: I suspend the Sitting and will take the Chair again at 4.15 pm.

speaker: Mdm Speaker
text: Sitting accordingly suspended  at 3.48 pm until 4.15 pm.

speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
text: This Bill is of great interest to me as the number of the prudential safeguards sought in the Bill are relevant to the circumstances in which I took over Punggol East SMC following the 2015 General Election.

speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
text: Many of the points that I intended to make have already been said by PRPTC Chairman Mr Zainal Sapari and I will not repeat them.

speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
text: I will confine my remarks to the Bill to these prudential safeguards.

speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
text: The last amendment of the Town Councils Act took place in 2005 and one of the changes which was effected then was the creation of an offence for the usage of funds in a manner not specifically authorised by the Act.

speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
text: The change was intended to, in the words of the then Minister of State Mr Heng Chee How, "to strengthen corporate governance of Town Councils going forward".

speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
text: That was and remains a very relevant goal.

speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
text: There is much public interest in and scrutiny of the way public bodies conduct themselves these days.

speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
text: It keeps the Government and public entities on their toes.

speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
text: This interest and scrutiny are even more pronounced when matters relating to public funds are concerned and I believe it is the right thing that we hold ourselves to the highest standard when it comes to stewardship of public money.

speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
text: While these are improvements over the current provisions, the provision set out in clause 9 of the Bill does not quite seem to go far enough.

speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
text: On this point, I seem to strangely be in complete agreement with Ms Sylvia Lim.

speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
text: The Bill requires a Town Council member's interest to be recorded in the register of interest and for the Town Council staff to refrain from exercising the relevant power until the Town Council has been given approval.

speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
text: What appears to be missing is an element of public accountability in the sense that these conflicts can be approved by the Town Council itself without input from MND or HDB.

speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
text: Knowing that conflicts of interest are to be publicly scrutinised is something which would be beneficial to the governance structure of the Town Councils.

speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
text: In addition, requiring a third party to approve conflicts of interest will avoid any allegations of whitewashing of conflicts of interest which may otherwise arise.

speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
text: Clause 14 of the amendment Bill proposes a change to set out clearly the relationship between Town Councils and statutory authorities and would require Town Councils to comply with certain directions of the authorities.

speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
text: While Town Councils are run autonomously, they are not autonomous self-governing regions which are not subject to the laws of the land.

speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
text: Town Councils were constituted to serve a specific purpose for the residents living within a particular town.

speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
text: The Town Councils Act deems members, officers and employees of Town Councils to be public servants for the purpose of the Penal Code.

speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
text: Whilst this confers certain additional protections, it does mean that they are, in certain respects, held to the highest standard than the man-in-the-street.

speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
text: They should also not seek to frustrate the functions of Government bodies by being uncooperative or non-responsive.

speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
text: This would certainly help encourage the leadership of Town Councils to provide all necessary cooperation to various Government agencies.

speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
text: The last thing you would want in the middle of an investigation is to be stonewalled.

speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
text: And the possibility that the Chairman or Secretary will be personally liable will certainly encourage them to get the Town Council to act more expeditiously or to cooperate with Government agencies charged with fact-finding.

speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
text: The final change I would like to speak about is clause 20 of the amendment Bill which amends the provisions of the Town Councils Act relating to financial reporting.

speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
text: The current version of the Town Council Act already provides for the implementation of financial rules but the amendment Bill gives them bite.

speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
text: Again, this is a welcomed change and now puts the rules on a statutory footing.

speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
text: The proposed power of inspection and the power to require compliance reviews are also a welcome change.

speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
text: Town Councils which are managed properly should not be too concerned with these.

speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
text: And the changes will provide residents in the town with confidence that the Government is able to intervene, at an early stage, if there are concerns about governance in the town.

speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
text: On the contrary, it imposes an equal burden on all Town Councils.

speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
text: There are currently 16 Town Councils, 15 of which are run by PAP.

speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
text: The changes to the Town Councils Act apply equally to PAP-led Town Councils as they do to AHTC which is led by WP.

speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
text: The Government is actually raising standards in respect of conflicts of interest, financial reporting and general prudential matters.

speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
text: There is no free pass given to the PAP or the WP Town Councils.

speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
text: The amendment Bill is a clear demonstration of a commitment to clean governance which has always been one of this Government's guiding principles.

speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
text: What is of singular importance at the end of the day is that the public interest is preserved and that public funds are safeguarded even if it comes at the expense of more stringent requirements on the part of persons who are directly involved.

speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
text: I would be surprised if any Member would disagree with this objective.

speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
text: Mr Pritam Singh, if I heard him correctly, implied that the Town Councils (Amendment) Bill amendments are targeted at WP politically, and that it gives advantage to the PAP Town Councils.

speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
text: But that episode simply demonstrates how the existing framework and legislation were insufficient to protect the public good or the interest of residents in Punggol East.

speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
text: The Government surely cannot be expected to sit back and let this sort of event take place a second time.

speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
text: The Government would be remiss in its duty to Singaporeans if it allowed what happened to Punggol East to ever happen again.

speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
text: There is also an implication by both Mr Pritam Singh and Ms Sylvia Lim that MND may not be neutral but may be partisan and will favour PAP Town Councils.

speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
text: I think this is merely a red herring.

speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
text: I can say with a high level of certainty that if AHTC held itself to the same high standards to which other Town Councils adhered to and conducted their affairs, with the same concern for proper governance as the PAP Town Councils, they would not have issues with MND.

speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
text: MND is acting in the interest of the public and not in the interest of PAP.

speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
text: While there are lapses in governance, even in the Prime Minister's constituency, as mentioned by Ms Sylvia Lim, these will be highlighted and dealt with transparently and decisively.

speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
text: In addition to Mr Low Thia Khiang successfully running HTC, Mr Chaim See Tong ran Potong Pasir Town Council for many years, over two decades, without running into the same sort of mess which AHTC now finds itself.

speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
text: KPMG, an independent professional firm, has also used very strong language in describing the affairs at AHTC.

speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
text: It appears that some progress has been made.

speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
text: But should all these points have arisen in the first place?

speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
text: With that, Mdm Speaker, I would strongly support the Bill.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: In his speech, he was making a vague reference to AHTC's handling of funds vis-a-vis Punggol East.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: I am not sure what he is complaining about.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: Is he still sticking to the statements he made during the election campaign that $22.5 million worth of sinking funds handed over to us have been unaccounted for?

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: He mentioned that AHTC has control failures and that these control failures should not have happened in the first place.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: Is he saying that PRPGTC has no observation points in their annual audits from the auditor?

speaker: Mr Charles Chong
text: Pasir Ris-Punggol and other Town Councils may have comments on it but none so bad as AHTC.

speaker: Mr Charles Chong
text: We have so many agencies, the Courts and so on putting their concerns in.

speaker: Mr Charles Chong
text: But we are going through the accounts to ascertain if there are more funds owed to us.

speaker: Mr Charles Chong
text: And we will let them know in due course after the auditors have examined their latest statement of accounts which we received only on 24 February this year.

speaker: Mr Charles Chong
text: On the amount that was transferred to us, they had returned us $20 million which we had transferred to them.

speaker: Mr Charles Chong
text: But in the two and half years that Punggol East was under control by them, they have not been able to account for it until just a short time ago, 24 February.

speaker: Mr Charles Chong
text: And even then, I think they have submitted three sets of accounts to us at different times, and all of those indicated that they had owed in sinking funds more than $4 million to $5 million.

speaker: Mr Charles Chong
text: And I think that money would not have been transferred if we had not served our letter of demand on them.

speaker: Mdm Speaker
text: Let us not convert this into a debate on the specific issues.

speaker: Mdm Speaker
text: But this is a debate on the general principles of the Bill.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: Yes, Mdm Speaker, I recognise that but Mr Charles Chong has made certain insinuations which have to be corrected in the public interest.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: With regard to the comments made about financial statements which had been given to PRPGTC but then taken back by AHTC, the first set of accounts putting up the position of Punggol East SMC was handed over to Pasir Ris Punggol on 27 September 2016.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: There were issues in there which PRPGTC wanted to meet AHTC to clarify.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: We did arrange for a meeting and our auditor actually met with officials from PRPGTC on 14 November.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: I am a bit surprised to hear about these, almost complaints about "Look, the money has not been given" and so forth.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: It is not very much longer than the final transfer that we have just made yesterday.

speaker: Mr Charles Chong
text: Okay, I am equally surprised that Mr Pritam Singh is unaware of it.

speaker: Mr Charles Chong
text: I think, as the Member mentioned, the first set of accounts that they sent to us in 2016, we found so many discrepancies that we sent it back.

speaker: Mr Charles Chong
text: After the meeting, which was called and discussed, they agreed that there were discrepancies and, therefore, they withdrew that set of accounts.

speaker: Mr Charles Chong
text: We are still trying to ascertain whether that is accurate, and it is a qualified account by the way.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information and Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: This point is not about the principles of the debate, but I have to clarify a comparison that Mr Pritam Singh is making, where the delay in transfer from PRPGTC to AHTC is being compared with the reverse transfer.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information and Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The reasons for the delay in both cases are quite different.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information and Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: In the first instance, where there was a delay of transfer to the new Punggol East Town Council under WP, the issue was about an agreement about the terms and conditions and the liabilities and so forth.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information and Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The delay in the other direction, which Mr Charles Chong has just talked about, is as a result of what has happened under the WP Punggol East Town Council, we were unable to ascertain how much should be transferred in the first place.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information and Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: There was a discrepancy between the first and the third sets of accounts that the WP themselves had submitted, so they were unable to ascertain, I believe, how much they should be transferring to us.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information and Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: If they were able to ascertain how much they were transferring to us, then there was no reason for it to be in three tranches, the last of which was only a few days ago, after the most recent sets of accounts.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information and Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: So, the comparison between those two sets of delays is entirely false.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information and Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: There was a delay on both sets, but the comparison is entirely false, because the reasons for the delay are entirely different.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: Yes, it is good to know that Minister of State Janil recognises that there was a delay for both different occasions, but the fact remains that the reason why those accounts were withdrawn was because Pasir Ris-Punggol said there were some problems with them.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: And in the right spirit, I believe we told the auditors: "Come, let's sit down.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: So, I am not sure what is so objectionable to the Minister of State Janil.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I am encouraged by the new section 19(4) curbing substantial trading or financial activities.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This new addition reinforces the spirit of the Act: that Town Councils should not lose sight of its core objectives, which is to manage the living conditions of residents and not take on ancillary activities which may not necessarily contribute directly to the interests of residents.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Next, with regard to the interaction between Town Councils and Statutory Boards, which many members have highlighted, according to section 21A, Town Councils must comply with any directions from Statutory Boards, so long as the directions belong to the broad categories listed in the section, and failure to comply would result in criminal conviction.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: While this section ensures that Statutory Boards may carry out their work efficiently, it does not appear to provide any firm platform for Town Councils to raise their concerns or reject a direction from a Statutory Board on reasonable grounds.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Next, I note that the Minister may pass model by-laws, and Town Councils can amend the model by-laws and pass its own by-laws.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: However, by-laws made by the Town Councils must not be "inconsistent" with the model by-laws.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The Bill further states that model by-laws could be made at any point in time.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I have no doubt that by-laws set by the Minister or Ministry would be done in the best interests of the residents.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: However, we need to have sight of what the model by-laws would be and knowledge of whether consultations and the frequency under which these would take place.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: As Members of this House are aware, different Town Councils may adopt different calculation methods of how much sinking fund is to be transferred, whether it be by number of blocks in precincts or by the unused balance sinking fund.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Over the past decade, if we look around us, there has been an increasing number of municipal councils around the world which have become insolvent, often, we must say, from factors beyond their direct control, for example, pension obligations, reductions in their traditional tax bases or even large lawsuits.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: One of the reasons is also that in many of these countries, there is a lack of regulatory oversight and also of intervention.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: All of these town councils do have some form of audit and, many times, the audits do show this inexorable deterioration in their finances, but nothing can be done in most of these cases because the government of the day of that country did not have the ability to step in and correct the cause when it had to be done.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: And so, it is here that I disagree with the WP position that we should just remain with the current state of affairs and rely on the AGO because that was the system that we had in the past.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Audits and surveillance are really no substitutes for regulation or the proper intervention, when needed.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Here, I take an example from a field that I am very familiar with.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: As a doctor working in a hospital, we have audits and we have heard that in other countries, for example, in the UK, when audits show deficiencies in care − which have led to problems of loss of life, to mobility for the patients − many of these cases, because there was no direct regulatory intervention, it took a long time before the audit results would go to the proper people so that the proper steps could be done.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: So, I think that this is the same situation here.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: There should be, in addition to an audit system or surveillance system, the proper regulation and also the intervention must be there to come in when needed, in this particular case, to safeguard the welfare and the benefits of the residents.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: The next question, of course, is: should MND not be the regulator?

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Well, if MND should not be the regulator, then who else should it be?

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I think it is a fallacious argument to always try to set up a new committee, which is supposedly independent, every time we need regulation.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I think we can suggest it in certain circumstances, but I do not think that is the way most governments work, because the whole thing becomes very unwieldy.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I also think we should give credit to the rule of law in Singapore and to our civil servants who perform their roles without fear or favour.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: If we keep on playing the persecution card and say that the cards are always stacked against us, there is no end to this argument and it is very hard for our nation to progress.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: That is why, in my opinion, MND is probably the best body in this particular case to step in when necessary, when Town Councils are in need of help.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I understand that MND adheres to the principle that Town Councils should remain autonomous entities, but that should not preclude them from some protections as, ultimately, it will be the residents who bear the consequences.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: For instance, municipalities in countries like Germany and Canada cannot become bankrupt, as their public debts are implicitly guaranteed by the state.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Could I ask that perhaps some considerations should be given to the fact that Town Councils could also be afforded some protections against claims?

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: For instance, limits can be imposed on certain of its liabilities.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I would also like to seek three further clarifications from the Minister.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: First, on the amendment of section 38 regarding the timely submission of audited accounts, in the event that the Town Council is in default and unable to produce the audited accounts and a fine is imposed, is this fine to be paid from the Town Council's coffers, or by the Committee or the Chairman of the Town Council?

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Second, with regard to section 31 − I know that Senior Minister of State Desmond Lee may have talked about it earlier − could I just confirm that Town Council staff and/or members of the MA will be barred from sitting on the Town Council Committee?

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: I am glad and fortunate to be living in Ang Mo Kio GRC, a precinct well-run by Dr Intan Azura.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: I truly believe in governance and accountability to every Town Council resident, for that matter.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: So, let me give a different perspective as a resident of a Town Council.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: This is to recognise that many lifts and lift parts need to be replaced before the end of the lifespan of the lift, as stipulated during the procurement phase.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: Otherwise, most, if not all the Town Councils, will not have sufficient sinking funds to do the replacement.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: As we debate the Town Council (Amendment) Bill, I have one suggestion and two clarifications for MND on points mentioned by the Senior Minister of State earlier.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: Although HDB procures the lifts while Town Councils maintain the lifts, I would like to suggest that HDB need to have a mindset that HDB has a large stake in maintaining the lifts.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: In this way, HDB will go all out to obtain feedback from the party that maintains the lift and incorporate the feedback when procuring the next batch of lifts.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: For example, HDB needs to take greater cognisance of the lifecycle costing of the lifts, compared to the purchasing cost of the lifts.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: In addition, HDB could also stipulate that the lift suppliers have a guarantee that all the lift spare parts, especially the parts that are under the sole proprietary right of the lift supplier, would be available throughout the lifespan of the lift at the inflation rate stipulated upfront.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: This will help to mitigate the issue of high lift maintenance costs and unavailability of spare parts.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: As for the clarifications, I note that under clause 18 (l) of the Bill, the Town Council can now transfer whole or part of the surplus of its operating fund at the end of a FY to LRF.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: Could I clarify whether the transfer of the surplus to LRF will also attract MND's co-funding even though the Town Council has already met its minimum obligation to transfer 40% of the operating revenue to the sinking fund?

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: Could I clarify if the Town Councils are obliged to contribute 40% of the $600 grant to the sinking fund?

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: If so, this will mean that the net grant by MND to offset the lift maintenance cost is only $360 per lift instead of $600.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: I hope the Minister can consider my suggestion and answer my two clarifications.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: (In Mandarin):   Mdm Speaker, I speak with a heavy heart as I join this debate on the Town Councils (Amendment) Bill.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: After the amendment, as the Chairman of a Town Council, I could go to jail if the Town Council is not managed appropriately.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: Why should I go to jail for mismanagement of the Town Council if I am not corrupt?

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: Town Councils manage funds running into hundreds of millions of dollars.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: Collected from the monthly S&CC paid by residents, these funds are the people's money and, of course, they should be well managed.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: The amendments this time will require the Town Councils to manage their funds properly and set out the accounts clearly.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: If a Town Council is not appropriately managed, its accounts not set out clearly, and it repeatedly disregards the authority's request to correct the errors by continuing to do what it did before, then the chairman will be prosecuted.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: MPs are representatives of the people, in charge of funds running into the millions, of course, they have the responsibility to run the Town Councils well.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: Some people may ask, why should MPs manage the Town Council?

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: Why not let the HDB manage the Town Councils directly?

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: Honestly, when managing a Town Council, MPs must manage things big and small.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: Projects worth millions of dollars must be examined carefully to see whether the tenderers are capable and the price is reasonable or not.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: It is also important to make sure there is no nepotism when awarding the contract, to avoid being accused of corruption.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: For small things, matters, such as complaints about neighbours throwing sanitary napkins from high floors, must also be handled.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: Some say, as representatives of the people, MPs just need to manage the big things of the country, and that the small things can be handled by the civil servants.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: It is said that whoever can be trusted in small things can be trusted in big things and whoever is dishonest in small things will be dishonest in big things, too.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: Those who do small things may not be able to do big things but those who cannot even do small things well cannot be expected to do big things.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: And this is the purpose of letting MPs run the Town Council.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: When an MP advocates transparency in Parliament, we must see whether accounts of the Town Council that he/she is managing are transparent and in order.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: When an MP says in Parliament we must greatly reduce foreign labour, we must also see whether his/her Town Council can do without even one foreign worker.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: When the MP says in Parliament that we shall not raise the price of anything, we must see whether his/her Town Council can, without raising S&CC, give annual increments to the Town Council's staff and cleaners, and pay for the ever-increasing lift maintenance cost.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: In other words, without raising S&CC, can the Town Council afford to pay for higher lift maintenance cost and annual increment of its staff without running into a deficit?

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: If, indeed, a deficit appears, how is it going to be tackled?

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: Running a Town Council is like running a local government.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: Clause 24 empowers the Town Councils to introduce by-laws.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: For example, the residents are not allowed to park or hold an event in certain areas.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: If an MP can manage the Town Council well whereby the public area is clean, the lifts are running smoothly and the accounts are kept orderly and balanced, then the people will feel assured that this MP can do bigger things, such as organising a government.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: But if an MP cannot manage the Town Council well, say the estate is not clean, the accounts are in a mess and every year there is a deficit, then how can we expect this MP to manage the country well?

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: I work in a listed company and I understand the importance of external auditing.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: If a listed company's accounts cannot pass external auditing, it means that the company's accounts are problematic and the shareholders will ask questions.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I have just quoted a passage from the Bill itself.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: One would be hard pressed to argue against having a stronger governance framework as this would only serve further to safeguard residents' interest and public funds from potential abuse and mismanagement.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I do believe many of my colleagues in the House have taken that point of view as well.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: While I do support this Bill, I would like to speak on two specific areas that in my opinion warrant closer scrutiny.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: My belief is that all collaboration between the Town Council and the other public agencies will always start with the right assumption that all agencies are working towards providing the best quality of service and benefits for residents, regardless of whichever Town Council or agency may be serving the residents in.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: This power should not be invoked in the first instance when there are differences in opinions of how duties are to be performed.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I would urge HDB and other public agencies to carefully study the merits of differing opinions offered by Town Councils before arriving at the conclusion that the powers proposed in the Bill should be invoked.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Also, Madam, I would like to comment on some speeches earlier which seem to suggest that perhaps the agencies, be it HDB, NEA or even MND, could be impartial or even biased in executing their services and duties, depending on the Town Councils they were serving.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: To do so would be a very unfair comment on some of our public agencies and our public officers.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I can honestly say that in my dealings with our agencies, it has not always been smooth.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I have had instances where we have had disagreements and different points of view.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: But to suggest that the officers in these public agencies are not capable of being unbiased, not capable of being fair in their judgement, would, to me, be an insult to these officers.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I would just like to state that for the record, Mdm Speaker.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I would also like to suggest that the Government also clarify the scope of responsibility of Town Councils and other public agencies when it comes to managing places that currently fall in areas where there are overlapping responsibilities.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: There was an incident that was an accident in my division a few weeks ago where a driver inadvertently reversed his car into the walls of a childcare centre at high speed and demolished the walls of the centre.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Thankfully, it was a weekend and the centre was closed because the place where the car ended up was where the children normally sleep.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: If it had happened the next day, I shudder to think of the consequences, Madam.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: We are now evaluating the design of the car park and all the car parks in our estate and plan to build safety bollards in car parks and/or void decks that have significant congregations of people where such accidents could possibly happen.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: The common areas in the void deck are being managed by the Town Council, the car park was designed and built by HDB.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Should HDB take responsibility even if the areas of the bollards that are to be constructed happen to be managed by the Town Council?

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I am sure that there are many such examples across the island and I hope there can be greater clarity on the scope of duties and responsibilities of Town Councils and public agencies in grey areas where the lines of responsibility are not so clearly delineated.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: The second point, Madam, is on clause 18 which is about the setting up of the sinking fund to cover the costs of lift replacement and lift upgrading works.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Given the large majority of residents in Singapore live in high-rise public housing, lifts can be viewed as a form of vertical public transport system that ferry people to their homes.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: A lift breakdown is extremely disruptive to residents' lives, especially for young children, the physically disabled and the elderly who might have trouble using the stairs.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: It is important that all these undergo regular maintenance services and the frequency of such preventive maintenance will only increase with the passage of time as lift parts get worn out at an exponential rate from age and heavy usage.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: To finance the growing needs to maintain and service the lifts, I agree that more Town Council funds should be set aside specifically for the purpose of lift maintenance and replacement.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I do believe this point was highlighted by Minister Lim Swee Say during the recent Committee of Supply (COS) debate.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I stress the aim must be to build a stronger Singaporean Core in this area of lift technicians and their similar skillsets and capability.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Strengthen the regulatory and corporate governance framework and benefit the residents.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: As such, I complete my speech in support of the Bill.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This House has broadly affirmed the need to strengthen Town Councils' public accountability and for the need for oversight on Town Councils.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Most issues and questions raised today pertain to the details of the proposed amendments and how they will play out in practice, whereas a few were far more fundamental in nature.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Both Mr Pritam Singh and Ms Sylvia Lim emphasised that they want the Town Councils' framework to be depoliticised.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: I have explained at the start of the debate what the purpose of the Town Council framework is.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And Mr Singh, on behalf of WP, accepts this premise.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The purpose of the Town Council framework is to establish a more direct nexus between elected Town Councillors, their management of Town Councils to deliver services in our housing estates and their resident-voters, and to allow our housing estates to develop a more distinctive character of their own, with direct involvement of their elected MPs, guided by the residents.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: As a political framework, Town Councils allow residents to see a side of their MPs that their performance in Parliament may not be able to demonstrate.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Here in this House, MPs speak, argue, persuade, contribute ideas, demonstrating their thoughtfulness, mental acuity, their oratorical skills and their sense of empathy and compassion, largely through speeches and ideas.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But in the day-to-day running of the Town Council as well as the estate, people can judge for themselves a different perspective − whether their MPs can really do things or not.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And is the Town Council financially sustainable and run honestly?

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: They can see for themselves the governance style and philosophy in action, and not just in word.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: So, for instance, MPs may espouse the virtues of openness and transparency but are they really practising what they preach when they run an organisation?

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: So, in short, Madam, the Town Council framework has served as a neutral training ground for MPs and political parties, to show whether they have what it takes to run a public entity and manage an estate and, by extension, the government and the country.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: More than 25 years on, the objectives of the Town Council still hold true.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: I am glad Mr Singh, on behalf of his Party, agrees with that.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: At the end of the day, if the Town Council is properly managed and the estate is well run, people may continue to support you at the ballot box, and the converse is equally true.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Allow me to reiterate the following key points.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Under the revised Act, Town Councils will continue to enjoy broad autonomy and be empowered to run their estates, as they have been for the past 28 years.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But these powers are not, and should not, be unfettered.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Town Councils will continue to exercise autonomy to run their estates, but within broad rules laid down to ensure proper governance and to safeguard public interest.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Autonomy does not give anyone a blank cheque to run down the Town Council or the estate, misuse funds, mismanage the system or break clearly established rules.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: In fact, some of the provisions in the Bill enhance the direct accountability that Town Councils are premised on, that is, accountability to residents and voters.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Town Councils are also required to keep long-term projections so that they have an honest opinion as to whether their management style is for the short term or for the long haul.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Unless the situation is so dire that the health or safety of residents is at risk, MND will not step into the shoes of Town Councils, which should do so as they are obliged to do.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: She says the new enforcement powers of the Town Councils (Amendment) Bill are too wide-ranging and may be wielded as a political tool because the Head of the Ministry is a political officeholder.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: These are serious allegations, quite unwarranted and, perhaps, are indicative of the world view from which the WP comes from.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: That when a political entity and a politician gets into power, there is no trust in his integrity, there is no trust in the voter, he must be checked, fettered, locked up, chained, that you need ombudsmen for every aspect of his work, especially when it relates to issues that may pertain to the politics of the land.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: First, let us all go back to fundamentals, and Mr Singh and Ms Lim are both lawyers, so they will understand this.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: When a government is elected by the people, political officeholders will helm the executive arm and be responsible for all the Ministries and agencies, including those that have law enforcement, regulatory and licensing powers, such as the Police, NEA, CPIB, the Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore and so on.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And we are not unique in that sense.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We are not a unique system to do this.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And as a Parliamentary majority, the Government can and is obliged to make laws in the public interest.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But, Madam, these powers and the laws that are made have to be used judiciously, fairly, justifiably and even-handedly.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: In the case of the Town Councils Act, they have to be applied across all Town Councils, regardless of political affiliation.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Some Members have spoken about how the Town Councils have been fined, some other Town Councils have been censured, embarrassed by agencies when they announced what has happened in the media, even the Prime Minister's Town Council.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: When allegations were made, they took the first step to make a report and now CPIB is investigating Ang Mo Kio Town Council.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Is there an allegation or claim that the officers of CPIB will fear investigating Ang Mo Kio Town Council?

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: I fear that the allegation goes a bit too far.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Because these powers, Madam, are derived from the people and given with their trust and confidence.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: There is no sweeping of things under the carpet.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Our history has shown that this Government, this Party, will act against wrongdoings.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: It will not sweep things under the carpet.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The recent Ang Mo Kio Town Council case is a case in point.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: In the event of a conflict of interest, there are established and appropriate ways to deal with it.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: If these powers are used in an unjustifiable manner for whatever reason, public trust will be seriously eroded.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We can certainly count on members of the Opposition acting as sentinels to make allegations every now and so often, pointing to shadows, claiming conspiracies.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Mr Pritam Singh and Ms Sylvia Lim called for the appointment of independent persons.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Mr Singh talked about independent auditor or accountant.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But these so-called independent ombudsman or independent accountants have to be appointed by somebody vested with the authority to take charge of the matter, somebody responsible for the policy of the issue.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: So, will the allegations of biasness and partisanship really ever end?

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: What about officeholders of other Ministries and agencies who may be responsible for the enforcement agencies or licensing agencies which might incidentally apply to Town Councils or to members of political parties, card-carrying members or to vocal pro-Opposition members?

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Does Ms Lim then say you need to have one law and one system for the common man and an independent ombudsman for all these other people that she has identified?

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Or should we have one law of the land and one system for everybody under the rule of law, under the scrutiny of the eyes of people and the protection of the Courts to ensure that the executive powers of the Government are exercised fairly?

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The whistle was first blown by AHPETC's own external auditors in 2011.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The subsequent audit was carried out by AGO, an independent audit office which Ms Sylvia Lim referred to in her speech.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: It made very serious findings about mismanagement, improper payments, conflict of interest, poor record-keeping and internal processes.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Equally serious conclusions were drawn by the Judiciary, both the High Court and the Court of Appeal, when the matter was brought to Court in 2015.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Pursuant to a Court order, AHTC appointed KPMG which came up with an independent report on the serious allegations of possible civil and criminal liability.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And now, at HDB's request, firm request if I may say so, and confirmed through a Court order by the Court of Appeal, AHTC has delegated decision-making on recovery of losses and further action to an independent panel comprising Mr Philip Jeyaretnam, Mr N Sreenivasan and Mr Ong Pang Thye, three eminent professionals.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: With the amendments to the Town Councils Act, none of these avenues and options will be abrogated.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: I certainly hope Mr Singh and Ms Lim do not also dispute the fairness and independence of these platforms.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: These inspectors, as I have said in my opening speech, must report to both MND as regulator and the Town Council over whom the review or investigations are being carried out.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: In most instances, consistent with the political philosophy underlying Town Councils, we expect that the Town Councils will, in a light touch scenario, on their own accord, resolve issues identified by the inspectors promptly.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: When an investigation needs to be carried out, MND is prepared to appoint independent auditors and professionals to carry out investigations and they will then have to report both to MND and the Town Council, as required by law.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Having said all this, perhaps let us go back and ask what really is AHTC's position on regulatory oversight?

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Is it, as I said earlier, a cynical fear that people who step up into politics and are elected by people into government are to be distrusted, that they will, in full glare of the public, misuse laws?

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Or was it really the case that Ms Lim is concerned about real problems being investigated by MND?

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: HDB applied for the Court to oversee this, the Court to appoint an auditor and for this auditor to be an independent auditor, not reporting to HDB or MND, reporting to Court, acting professionally and independently.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: To our surprise, AHTC fought the application and tried to stop an independent auditor from being appointed by the Supreme Court of Singapore.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Their lawyer argued explicitly in Court with his client behind him on AHTC's behalf that even if there was mismanagement of misspent funds, their view was that there was nothing that could be done, other than through the ballot.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: So, is it a willingness for appropriate independent, fair, justifiable regulatory oversight, or is there a preference for no oversight whatsoever?

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Apart from the public eye, there is always the recourse of the Courts under the framework of judicial review.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Ours is a system where the rule of law and any abuse of public powers are subject to the jurisdiction of the Courts.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: I am sure Mr Singh and Ms Lim understand that very well.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This has been a difficult two weeks for public officers.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: First, some claimed that they have no heart; and now, they have a black heart.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: They understand the imperatives, they understand the need for fairness.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: They have their own mind and own heart and will act and do what is right.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And in MND, we have a team of public officers overseeing Town Council matters fulltime.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We have no doubt that these officers will carry out their duties professionally and objectively in serving the interests of residents and Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: I am told that the Secretariat wrote to the Town Council to point out certain errors and mistakes which were not publicly disclosed.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Next, I would address questions posed by different Members on specific regulatory powers, why they were introduced and the mechanisms for enforcement.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: A few MPs have sought clarifications on the penalty provisions.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Dr Chia Shi-Lu asked if fines against Town Councils will be paid out of Town Councils' funds.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This is no different from how Town Councils, companies and charities pay for fines imposed by other agencies for regulatory infringements.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Mr Lim Biow Chuan sought clarity on what key decision-makers would be held personally liable for an offence.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: There are penalty provisions under the existing Town Councils Act that hold key decision-makers in the Town Councils, such as the Chairperson and Secretary, liable for offences committed by the Town Council with their consent and connivance.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This treatment will be extended to the new offences under the amended Act.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Mr Zainal Sapari suggested making it mandatory for Town Councils to purchase professional liability insurance, to provide protection from claims arising from the negligence of key decision-makers.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: There is nothing to stop a Town Council from purchasing such insurance, if they see value in doing so.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: It is a new power that gives the regulator the opportunity to have a gradation of remedies and actions and levers, depending on the severity of the infraction.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Ms Sylvia Lim asked about the conflict of interest provision that is embedded in the Bill which disqualifies people who have significant influence over the MA from being appointed to key officers in a Town Council.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The legislation is quite clear on this phrase.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But Ms Sylvia Lim talked about the GM of the Aljunied Town Council, from I think CPG or one the subsidiaries, when she took over.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Back then, under the Financial Reporting Standards (FRS), CPG would not be a related party but FM Solutions and Services (FMSS) would be because of the personal direct pecuniary financial interest that both Ms How Weng Fan and the late Mr Danny Loh held in the MA.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: So, I think that makes it quite clear.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Members also sought clarification on the code of governance.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: MND will introduce this code of governance in consultation with Town Councils.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Amongst other objectives, the code promulgates greater transparency and accountability in Town Councils' decision-making by setting out principles of good governance and highlighting best practices that can guide the Town Councils in executing their fiduciary responsibilities and improve accountability and disclosure.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This code is likely to take some reference from provisions in the code of governance for charities and institutions of a public character and the code of corporate governance for companies and may cover the principles and mechanisms to ensure independent decision-making and manage potential conflicts of interest.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Practices that ensure robust risk management and well-documented internal controls, systems and policies to protect stakeholders' interests and to safeguard Town Councils' assets.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This is within the remit of Town Councils' role to manage common properties, subject to the rules.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: As mentioned, this does not prevent the Town Councils from investing in stocks, funds and securities with advice from a qualified person or licensed body, subject to the existing safeguards in the TCFRs.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: To allay Mr Darryl David's and Mr Lim Biow Chuan's concerns, the requirements for Town Councils to cooperate with public agencies, cater to scenarios where Town Councils unreasonably prevent a Government agency from carrying out its statutory duties in HDB estates.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This is a rather extreme scenario and we do not expect this to be an ordinary occurrence.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: While there are challenges on the ground, by and large, Town Councils and agencies have worked well.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The key is that parties involved maintain open communications and work together to find solutions that best serve the residents.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Notwithstanding that, the amendments provide an avenue for MND to intervene when critical works are delayed or hampered at the expense of residents' safety, health and well-being.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: To be clear, this provision only kicks in when a Town Council unreasonably refuses to grant access or support where public health, public safety and order are at stake.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Other statutory authorities have also met with resistance from some Town Councils on the installation of monitoring devices like surveillance cameras and the maintenance of common property.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: That same Town Council also refused to repair a resident's letterbox.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: They wanted HDB to require all residents to sign an undertaking to maintain their own letterboxes.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: If they refused to sign it, the Town Council wanted HDB to hand over a copy of every resident's mailbox key to the Town Council, a request that was turned down by HDB.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Some Town Councils raised questions when the Land Transport Authority stopped paying the Temporary Occupation Licence (TOL) fees for traffic monitoring equipment installed on HDB rooftops.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Some of these incidents were amicably resolved after MND stepped in but other cases simply failed to find proper closure.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Before I end this point, I would like to address Ms Sylvia Lim's concerns that this Bill somehow gave the impression that the Town Council is always wrong and the public authorities are always right.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: It is a public authority, a public body constituted by an Act of Parliament, but it is also a statutory body with political characteristics, a point which I think WP also accepts.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The public agencies responsible for public health, public safety and public order are national authorities charged with very important functions.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The first approach will be and has always been to discuss the matter with the Town Council.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: For instance, if NEA needs to prevent killer-litter and needs to put in a camera, they will ask the Town Council and tell them they need to put it here for whatever reason.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And if there are legitimate reasons why the Town Council refuses, then the agencies and the Town Council should discuss.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: If the Town Council, for whatever reasons, still refuses and believes that it is correct, then it should fight the matter in Court, let the judge decide as to whether the Town Council had reasonable cause to refuse to comply with the compliance order.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Mr Louis Ng also asked in this regard if the Town Council would have a platform to raise concerns or reject a compliance directive by statutory authorities.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: In my earlier response to Ms Syvia Lim, I have shown that this, in fact, would be woven into the process.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Mr Louis Ng asked about the model by-laws.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: To clarify, the intent to scope these by-laws narrowly is so as not to fetter the autonomy of Town Councils.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Town Councils will still have autonomy to set the by-laws.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But the provisions in the model by-laws would only relate to certain aspects of the management of common property, such as rules on damage of common property or the erection of unauthorised structures on common property.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: These are areas where although we want Town Councils to set their own rules and have flexibility, there are certain areas where we would need uniformity for national purposes.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: These by-laws will provide a common baseline for all Town Councils to build upon and ensure that there is some consistency in the management of common properties across towns.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: I would next address points made on the provisions relating to the financials of Town Councils, raised by a number of Members of this House.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The Bill pushes Town Councils to regularly review their long-term financial health, and most, if not all, the Members who spoke support this intent and I thank them.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: I fully agree with Dr Chia Shi-Lu that we should avoid a situation where a Town Council becomes financially insolvent, as it will ultimately be the residents who will bear the consequences.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This is why we have, in the Bill, focused on pre-emptive measures.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: By putting in place mechanisms for Town Councils to prepare their long-term financials and as a reality check for themselves to review their financial positions regularly.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This includes the appointment of independent advisors to advise the Town Council on the management of its affairs, with the hope that it will turn the ship around.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: As for Dr Chia Shi-Lu's suggestion on having the state guarantee all the debts of Town Councils, we will have to study very carefully how the examples he cited in Germany and Canada do it, while avoiding, I hope, the problems of serious moral hazard.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We certainly do not want Town Councils to take on more risks than necessary, in the belief that the Government will bail them out should things go wrong.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Mr Ang Wei Neng asked whether Town Councils can be allowed not to set aside part of the Lift Maintenance Grants to their LRFs.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: To clarify, this grant, like other grants provided to the Town Councils, are meant both for immediate need as well as for long-term use.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: So, even in lift maintenance, there are both immediate maintenance and repair needs, and more long-term replacement, maintenance needs that may require it to be split into the two accounts, that is, operating and the sinking fund types of accounts.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But we will take Mr Ang's suggestions and concerns into account.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Members have highlighted that on the ground and in practice, the responsibilities of Town Councils vis-a-vis other agencies and each other may be fuzzy, and good partnership is key.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Not everything can be clarified in legislation, which articulates broad frames and principles.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Sharp delineations of turf are often not possible and sometimes may lead to perverse outcomes.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: In areas where there is less clarity, I urge Members to be guided by what would most benefit residents.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Where there are gaps, we will continue to work with Town Councils and Town Councillors to clarify mutual or overlapping responsibilities, as we have done with handover guidebooks, circulars and the Code of Governance that we will be developing in consultation with Town Councils.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Several Members, including Dr Teo Ho Pin, Mr Zainal Sapari and Mr Louis Ng, among others, suggested that MND introduce more specific guidelines and rules to facilitate handovers between Town Councils following an Election.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: A smooth changeover of Town Councils ensures continuity in services to residents.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: In 2013, we developed a Town Council handing-over/taking-over guide in consultation with various Town Council Chairmen.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The guide clarifies some of the points raised today, such as the respective roles and responsibilities of the handing-over and taking-over of Town Councils and includes a checklist of the matters to be mutually agreed upon by the two Town Councils. "Mutually agreed upon" is an important phrase.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We circulated the guide to Town Councils before the 2015 General Election to provide a clear and easy reference for changeover of Town Councils.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This is not new as MND has already been making such Town Council orders after elections.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Nevertheless, there are some amendments to the existing provisions to provide greater clarity and guidance, such as, first, clarifying what happens in exceptional scenarios when the election results of some constituencies are delayed, for instance, due to the need to tally overseas votes.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Second, to clarify that the Minister can require an outgoing Town Council to furnish all the necessary information and documents relating to the transfer of an estate to the taking-over Town Council.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This is still work-in-progress and we will take into account Members' feedback as we continue to look into how we can better facilitate Town Council handovers going forward.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Notwithstanding these improvements, the willingness of both sides to cooperate with each other on the transfer of the assets and information is key to a seamless transition.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The legislative requirements have been kept broad because not every detailed situation can be anticipated, and to also allow Town Councils some latitude to discuss the issues that arise and to reach an amicable resolution that benefits their residents.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Nevertheless, if there are irreconcilable differences in opinion, MND can and has facilitated discussions between Town Councils and made itself available to mediate any differences.

speaker: Mdm Speaker
text: Senior Minister of State, we should ask the Leader to move a Motion to extend your time?

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: A moment ago, I talked about the handover between Town Councils.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Now, I am talking about the handover from HDB of new BTOs to Town Councils.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We accept there is always room to do better.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: HDB is continually seeking to improve its handover processes with Town Councils.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: As Members know, HDB has developed a handover procedure booklet which details various proposed improvements to the handover process.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: After that, HDB will arrange for a briefing to the Town Council on the essential mechanical and electrical (M&E) systems that are developed.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We hope Town Councils will give HDB their feedback and work with HDB to refine the procedures, which we will continue to improve along the way.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Various members also raised concerns about the performance of lifts in HDB estates.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We have covered this fairly comprehensively during MND's Committee of Supply (COS) debate a few days ago.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: In essence, our approach is to ensure that our lifts remain safe and reliable, an approach which requires multi-pronged support from the Building and Construction Authority (BCA), HDB, Town Councils and the industry.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: As I have said at MND's COS, as our estates age, all of us, including Town Councils, will need to do more in maintaining and replacing our estate infrastructure, such as lifts, facades, water tanks and roofs, so that our estates remain liveable and safe.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: It is easy to build and continue to build and to agree to requests to build.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: It is less attractive to talk about the long tail of maintenance.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But let us accept that this is an essential part of city living.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Since Town Councils bear the responsibility for the eventual replacement of estate infrastructure and such expenditures could be large and backloaded, Town Councils need to take a longer-term view of their finances, plan ahead and start saving today for the expenditures.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: A good example is the maintenance and replacement of lifts, which many Members talked about.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Many of the costs are backloaded, occurring beyond 2025.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: So, therefore, while Town Councils' current sinking fund balances, which may total up to $1 billion, seem healthy, they are not sufficient to cover the cost of future lift replacements, let alone other works like cyclical repainting and replacement of other key infrastructure.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Last September, we asked Town Councils to give us a sense of their financial projections over the next 10, 20, 30 years.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We accept that the further you look ahead, the less reliable are your projections.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The Town Councils are aware that at their current levels of income and sinking fund contribution rates, they are unlikely to have sufficient funds for the replacement costs for the long term.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Some may even fall into deficits even earlier.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: That is why we have reviewed the Town Councils' projections and announced some changes earlier.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: As the chart on the screen shows, Town Councils will have to set up a dedicated LRF, which will be created by this Bill, that is ring-fenced for the replacement of lifts and lift parts.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The minimum contribution rate for the LRF could have been higher if we had sized it based on a full lifecycle costing approach for lifts, a point which Mr Ang Wei Neng had asked about.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: However, we decided to ease in the changes for Town Councils and provide significant Government financial support to help Town Councils and residents with these costs.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: MND had earlier announced the set of new grants and measures to provide additional financial support for Town Councils.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: First, a $450 million Lift Enhancement Programme over 10 years to help Town Councils fund the cost of lift enhancements.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Second, additional matching grants to match half of Town Councils' quarterly contributions to their LRFs to help Town Councils build up their LRF more quickly.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This will cost over $50 million a year to the Government.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Third, a Lift Maintenance Grant to help Town Councils cope with higher lift-related servicing and maintenance costs, estimated at about $13 million a year.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: While the Government has taken the lead to share significantly in the costs of maintaining and replacing estate infrastructure, this is very much a shared responsibility.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Town Councils need to do their part, to plan our finances, start saving now and gradually build up our sinking funds and LRF over time.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This is a responsibility for all Town Councils to do.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We have seen how the dynamics have played out in private condominium estates.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Immediate pressures from residents at annual general meetings (AGMs) to cause Management Corporation Strata Titles (MCSTs) to kick the can down the road and avoid raising their sinking fund contributions.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But when there are major estate infrastructure works, these MCSTs find themselves unable to carry them out.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: All residents living at that point in time at the estate will then have to cough up a tremendously large amount of money to replace, say, a lift or an old water tank.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This is not how we should operate in our public estates.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We should prepare and save for our collective future and not kick the can down the road, with everyone contributing their fair share towards improving our living environment rather than leave future generations to bear the costs.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: First, the new provision holds Town Councils to higher standards of governance, transparency and accountability in carrying out their duties.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This is the right thing to do and Singaporeans expect this of Town Councils.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: At the same time, the Bill puts in place a system for regular reporting and calibrated actions along with the necessary levers for enforcement.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: These will allow more timely and effective interventions to be taken when residents' interests are put at risk.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But recent developments suggest that we cannot assume that MPs will always act in the residents' best interests.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Our Town Councils continue to have broad autonomy and latitude in deciding how best to manage the estates under their charge.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The Government also has a responsibility to put in place a framework of good governance and accountability, and to request for information, investigate and intervene when the trust is breached or when things go wrong.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
