text: Taking a light-touch approach does not mean that the Government adopts a no-touch policy.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: At the end of the day, the Government's overriding considerations must be to safeguard residents' interests and public funds.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This Bill will set a strong foundation for the good governance of our Town Councils, taking into account developments over the years and building on 28 years of experience operating Town Councils.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: Earlier in his speech, he alluded to the Court case which MND brought against AHPETC and the position that we took at the time.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: But in this case, what Part IVA is expecting HDB employees, for example, who are appointed as inspectors, to do is to possibly make adverse findings against their political masters.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: The investigation will be triggered by the Minister for National Development himself.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: While he may want to do the right thing or the public servants may want to do the right thing, the reality is such.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: I think those of us who are realists will know the problem.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: Thirdly, regarding the issue of whether MND is the proper entity to implement or to supervise Town Councils as such, as the Senior Minister of State has repeated many times, fundamentally, Town Councils are political institutions.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: To vest a political officeholder with the decision-making power over political institutions, is just not tenable.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: As I mentioned in my speech, it is not just my view, but it is also the view of some corporate governance observers who have mentioned that, at least in terms of perception, it just does not look right.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: He also mentioned that MND has also been so-called quite nice to AHTC by writing to us to tell us that our accounts, maybe there are some things that we need to clarify but, at the same time, we see a media release yesterday, nicely timed for today's debate.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: So, this is just another example of the Ministry's behaviour.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: I am not too clear about what the Senior Minister of State meant regarding the conflicts of interest and the C-suite, which he talked about in his opening speech.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: Currently, the way the provisions are worded, so long as this person has a significant influence over the business of the MA, that person would not be able to be a Town Council Secretary or GM.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: The point is, is it just the Chief Executive Officer (CEO)?

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: AHTC, when it was brought to Court, was asked to respond to an application by MND to let the Court appoint an independent auditor to look into its difficulties.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: It was not a case of MND asking the Court to allow MND to go in.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: It was MND asking the Court to appoint an independent auditor.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The first key point that struck us was that AHPETC or AHTC resisted that Court application as framed.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The point about MND being found by the Court not to be the right party had nothing to do with this point about whether anything could be done if there was mismanagement.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: It was purely based on the Court's reading of whether it was MND or HDB, and ultimately, they said it was HDB.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And HDB made the application to the Court of Appeal.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The key point I would like this House to take away is that while Ms Sylvia Lim talked aspirationally about the need for independence, an independent oversight, what the Town Council was arguing in Court was that, where there was mismanagement of funds, nothing could be done beyond the ballot box.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The second point was about civil servants and about whether they are prepared to make adverse findings against political masters, I think she has just contradicted herself.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: First, she says on the one hand, she said her former colleagues are people of integrity and of spine and steel, and will do what is right, as is the ethos of this Public Service.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And on the other, in a backhanded way, she says they will kowtow their timorous souls.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: In fact, that is what she is saying.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Our officers are brought up with an ethos of integrity, service and excellence.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: There is, indeed, now ongoing, a CPIB investigation into certain individuals, or an individual in the Ang Mo Kio Town Council.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: What is Ms Lim's analogy extending to that case going to be?

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Third, MND being political because the Minister is a politician and that Town Councils are political and, therefore, the Ministry should not be a regulator.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The Ministry has been the regulator for 28 years.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: As to conflict of interest, Madam, we have to decide where to draw the line.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Where there is a conflict of interest, the first basis, the first thing you do, is to declare it, have it registered and recuse yourself.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Do not take part in the decision because you are conflicted.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But we have gone much further to say that if you are a person wielding significant influence over the MA, you are not allowed to occupy key offices in the Town Council.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We have to strike a balance between a recusal process and an absolute prohibition.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And I think we have taken a high-water mark.

speaker: Mdm Speaker
text: Ms Lim, we are going around in circles, as you can see.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: I think what the Senior Minister of State is responding to is that he is saying that under Part VIA, if the Minister should instruct so, the AGO may be activated.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: Fundamentally, to ensure an even keel and uniform standard throughout all the Town Councils, we see great value in getting the AGO to do rotational audits of Town Councils, whether or not the Minister triggers them.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: In Part IVA, there are two kinds of interventions.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: In the latter, I have explained to Mr Pritam Singh that in regard of the investigation into Town Councils, it will be carried out by independent professionals.

speaker: Mdm Speaker
text: Ms Lim, do you wish to record your dissent?

speaker: Mdm Speaker
text: Can those who wish for their dissent to be recorded please stand up?
